title: PR 5678 - KV Cache & Batching Refactor - review scratchpad
content:
Quick notes / brain dump while reviewing PR #5678 (kv-cache + batching refactor). Mostly TODO/checklist and file-level pointers. This is a rough scratchpad - will consolidate into a tidy PR comment before finalizing.

Overview:
- Goal: simplify KV cache lifecycle + unify batching strategy across CPU/GPU paths. Claim: ~15% p99 token latency improvement in nightly perf runs.
- Changes touch: cache manager, request router, batch scheduler, model inference loop, unit + integration tests.
- Author: @luis-ortega. Tests included but several smoke tests are flaky locally.

High-level concerns (need confirm):
- Backwards compatibility: ensure cache serialization format unchanged or migration provided. There is a small bump in header version but no migration code - ask author.
- Concurrency: cache eviction logic moved into async task - check for race with request path (look at cache_manager.py: evict_async).
- Error handling: router fallback behavior probably OK but confirm metrics emitted on fallback path.
- Perf metrics: the CI perf runs show improvement but variance high; need reproducible microbench.

Review checklist (to turn green):
- [ ] Unit tests pass locally (run pytest -k cache && pytest tests/integration/test_batching.py)
- [ ] Add deterministic microbench harness for batch scheduler (job: perf/kvscheduler/bench)
- [ ] Validate cache serialization versioning + add migration or guard (if header.version mismatch -> rebuild kv)
- [ ] Add comment explaining why we moved eviction off the hot path (latency tradeoff)
- [ ] Ensure we emit metrics: cache_evictions_total, cache_hit_ratio_by_model, batch_size_histogram
- [ ] Confirm no semantically breaking changes to public API (CacheManager.get/put signature)
- [ ] Fix flaky integration test test_batching_edge_case (seen on Linux/AWS)
- [ ] Add a small e2e test that reproduces the previously failing scenario: large prefix reuse + high concurrency

File-level notes (quick jump targets):
- runtime/cache/cache_manager.py
  - lines 120-180: new EvictionTask implementation. Potential race: EvictionTask._evict calls _delete without lock. Suggest holding self._lock or using compare-and-delete.
  - serialize()/deserialize(): header.version incremented from 1 -> 2. No migration path. Add a comment or migration helper.

- runtime/scheduler/batching.py
  - schedule_batch() changed to await on _flush_trigger instead of timer-based flush. Need to confirm behavior under low QPS (could increase latency). Add unit that simulates low QPS with long tails.
  - handle_batch_backpressure(): new logic that drops inflight small batches in favor of filling bigger ones. This is fine but docstring needs clearer rationale + metric for dropped_batches.

- runtime/inference/runner.py
  - _run_step: KV cache access moved before tokenization in some paths. Is that intentional? Might reduce cache hit because tokenization affects key. Add comment and tests.

- tests/*
  - test_cache_serialization.py: added new test for v2 header but it only asserts roundtrip for newly created v2 objects; we need migration test: deserialize old v1 bytes and assert rebuild is safe.
  - test_batching.py: a few skipped marks on CI; check skip reasons.

Refactor suggestions (non-blocking):
- Consider extracting EvictionTask into runtime/cache/evict.py with clear interface to simplify testing (makes it easier to run without full CacheManager).
- Move batching heuristics (size thresholds, timeouts) into config object with names (e.g., BatchPolicy) so we can A/B test in prod.
- The new compare-and-delete pattern used in cache lookups is copy-pasted in two files; factor into CacheUtils.atomic_delete(key, expected_value).

Testing / perf plan:
- Local repro: run bench_kv_cache.py with --seed 42 and capture p50/p95/p99 for baseline vs PR branch (use same docker image).
- Nightly: add perf job under ci/perf/pr/5678 that runs 3 trials and asserts no regression > 2% at p99.
- Add chaos test: heavy evictions under high concurrency to catch race conditions (simulate thousands of short lived requests).

Follow-ups / action items for author or owners:
- [Luis] Add migration or explicit destructive fallback on deserialize mismatch (JIRA-243).
- [Luis] Add a test that loads a real v1 serialized blob and confirms behavior (see linked_confluence page for schema).
- [Priya] Look into flaky test test_batching_edge_case - I can help reproduce on my macOS laptop.
- [Maya] Add perf harness and baseline runs; will post results to PR and perf channel.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the cache header bump intentionally a breaking change? If yes, it needs doc + release note.
- Does moving eviction off hot path change token latency SLAs for small requests? We need microbench on 1-token requests.
- Are batch dropping heuristics safe for low-latency tiers (tiered routing might prefer lower latency over throughput)? Might need config toggle per-customer-tier.

Notes-to-self (things to include in final PR comment):
- Summarize race findings and whether we require locks or atomics.
- Ask for explicit migration strategy or acceptance of clearing old caches on deploy.
- Recommend adding metrics and perf harness.
- If author prefers not to migrate v1, require release note and an opt-out config under "experimental.cache_v2".

Slack/links to paste into PR comment:
- perf runs: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/perf/5678/
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=98765
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-243

OK - will start by running pytest locally and then push a small comment to PR with the checklist. Add a couple inline comments for the evict race and serialization.

-- Maya
